we have developed a Cu2O-based PEC cell for low voltage H production that delivers a 78 % faradaic efficiency under −0.20 V bias potential.
we demonstrate that the combination of a NiFe-LDH co-catalyst with a Cu2O semiconductor electrode enables efficient low bias PEC water splitting.

the development of new materials for photo-electrochemical water-splitting.

the development of a new type of photoelectrochemical water splitting device based on a Cu2O photocathode and NiFe-LDH co-catalyst, which is able to produce H2 at a low applied voltage of −0.2 V vs Ag/AgCL.
the development of new materials for the efficient and sustainable production of clean energy.

the NiFe-Layer Double Hydroxide (LDH) is a promising co-catalyst for Cu2O-based photoelectrodes.
NiFe-LDH is an efficient co-catalyst for low bias water splitting on Cu2O photocathodes.
this work reports the first successful use of a NiFe-LDH as co-catalyst in a Cu2O photocathode.

the Cu2O/NIFe-LDH photocathode can be used to produce hydrogen under sunlight illumination at low bias condition.

we have demonstrated that the use of LDHs as a co-catalyst can significantly improve the performance of Cu2O in photoelectrochemistry, and this improvement is particularly significant at low voltage bias conditions.

the Cu2O/NIFLDH photocathode can be used for low bias PEC water splitting, which is an important step forward in view of the development of a self-biased photoelectrochemical cell for solar H2 production.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LDHs are a versatile and promising class of co-catalyst materials for PEC systems.
LDHs can act as efficient co-catalysts for Cu2O photoanodes in view of low voltage PEC water splitting.
NiFe-LDH is able to improve the electron transfer from Cu2O to the electrolyte, thus enabling the operation of the Cu2O-based photocathode at low bias conditions.
